strategy.summary: TestForge's axe scan found no violations on `/` and `/contact`, and no e2e test runs axe on either page yet. This change adds an axe check for each page as a new test in the spec that already covers it (tests/home.spec.js and tests/contact.spec.js), using @axe-core/playwright, which is already a devDependency. Each check fails on any violation of minor impact or worse, which covers every impact axe reports, and names each rule and the elements it failed on. The application and the existing tests are not changed, and the known violations on /about and /cart are left alone.
inScope: small shared helper tests/helpers/axe.js that runs axe and keeps the violations of minor impact or worse, as {id, impact, targets}
outOfScope: Known violations color-contrast on /about and image-alt on /cart (earlier runs reported them, their issues are open)
Keyboard and screen-reader behaviour, which axe cannot detect
assumptions: The real app runs for real: the existing Playwright webServer starts it with `node server.js` on port 4174. Nothing is faked.
The existing tests stay as they are. Each axe check is a new test in the spec file for its page.

The scan uses axe's default rule set, with no withTags, include or exclude, so every rule the TestForge scan ran is guarded. The work item says the pages pass at any impact, so the checks keep minor and worse.
